dossier.public_summary: The 0.69-day dip matches the star's own 0.688-day spot rotation period almost exactly, and the light curve outside the dips swings by more than the dip itself.

reasons.why: Phase-curve swing is larger than the transit depth itself with huge chi2, inconsistent with a planet and pointing to spots/variability or a close binary on the target.

Dip period equals the stellar rotation period to 0.000167 d, with ~2% FAP essentially zero and spot amplitudes ~22587-23456 ppm (~7x transit depth) in both sectors. This is the classic spot-modulation harmonic false alarm, matching outcome ambiguous/false alarm in similar candidates.

reasons.why: Duration 1.727x the central duration highly inconsistent with the host radius, requiring an extremely grazing low-density solution with density penalty 0.706 of the fit chi2. Stellar density mismatch positively favours stellar variability rather than a planet transiting an M dwarf.

reasons.why: Independent scorer ranks this well below the median planet (0.5), as expected for rotation-locked, out-of-density dips with no on/off-target discriminant to save them. The flat shape, no odd/even and no significant secondary do not outweigh the variability evidence.
